name: Lando Norris
assessment: An identity-specific accent can make a site recognisable before reading. Racing energy is appropriate to Norris; copying that urgency would misrepresent a reflective designer.

name: Messenger
assessment: A single playable task makes an imaginary world understandable. Use that clarity in an optional experiment; making visitors complete a game to see work adds friction.

name: Igloo Inc
assessment: A unified 3D world offers strong recall. Keep a consistent material language; infinite transitions are a poor trade for a small portfolio that needs direct comparison.

name: Don't Board Me
assessment: Graphic storytelling can establish a point of view. The lesson is conviction in one idea, not adopting a campaign’s visual rhetoric without its cause.

name: Opal Tadpole
assessment: Specific product imagery gives motion a subject. Treat portfolio artwork as evidence with a clear image hierarchy; avoid distortion that obscures the designed outcome.

name: Lusion v3
assessment: Spatial craft can itself demonstrate capability. Borrow the disciplined relationship between motion and composition, but a brand designer should still lead with brand work.

name: Noomo Agency
assessment: A studio can communicate through a continuous spatial narrative. Use continuity between pages; avoid a cinematic introduction that delays the portfolio.

name: Mana Yerba Mate
assessment: Illustrated commerce ties personality to product. Let existing project colours appear in their artwork rather than turning the whole portfolio into an unrelated illustration style.

name: KPR
assessment: Experimental worldbuilding fits an entertainment/community proposition. Its density would compete with the user’s identities; reserve discovery for the Playground.

name: The Other Side of Truth
assessment: Interaction can embody a serious editorial argument. In case studies, explain the problem and decision before celebrating the effect.

name: Persepolis Reimagined
assessment: 3D is strongest when it reveals otherwise inaccessible spatial information. A historical reconstruction is not a template for presenting flat brand artwork.

name: Pangram Pangram Foundry
assessment: Typography can be both the subject and interface. High relevance: strong type hierarchy and a catalogue visitors can scan without waiting.

name: Star Atlas
assessment: A game universe has a reason for cinematic scale. Low direct fit: worldbuilding would imply a game/3D specialism that is not the main portfolio proposition.

name: Prometheus Fuels
assessment: A process can become a spatial story. Use staged explanation when a case study warrants it; do not make a simple biography into a product launch film.

name: Umami Land
assessment: Exploration becomes meaningful when each discovery teaches something. Give experimental forms a short question and explicit controls.

name: Chungi Folio
assessment: A personal portfolio can make character visible through authored illustration and motion. High conceptual fit; the user needs his own motif rather than a borrowed cartoon voice.

name: Mammut Expedition Baikal
assessment: Photography and typography can carry an expedition’s drama. Let real project imagery provide variety; do not add fake cinematic footage to fill absent case material.

name: Kode Sports Club
assessment: Not assessed: the matching award record could not be verified. The collection title is inventory evidence only; no visual or interaction judgement is claimed.

name: Dark: Official Netflix Guide
assessment: An interactive guide can clarify relationships. Make project navigation and metadata systematic before introducing special transitions.

name: Synchronized studio
assessment: Monochrome typography leaves room for confident transitions. Strong relevance to Swiss structure; restrain choreography so the work remains quick to reach.

name: Pioneer - Corn Revolutionized
assessment: A difficult industrial process gives 3D explanatory purpose. Use process visuals only where the user can supply actual evidence of decisions.

name: Bruno Simon Portfolio
assessment: The interaction is an unmistakable demonstration of a creative developer’s skills. Excellent conceptual coherence, weak direct fit for a brand designer’s primary navigation.

name: MA
assessment: Distinct spatial worlds can help separate product families. A shared portfolio shell should stay consistent while each case study keeps its own artwork.

name: The Cool Club x FWA
assessment: A collection can feel like a set of physical objects. Apply numbering and catalogue rhythm, with conventional links rather than simulated handling requirements.

name: Nomadic Tribe
assessment: Illustrated narrative creates emotion through a coherent world. Low stylistic fit; its lesson is a governing idea, not maximal atmospheric production.

name: Orano
assessment: Spatial narrative can make an abstract industry legible. Retain the explanation-first principle and avoid production spectacle without information gain.

name: koox
assessment: Minimal structure and illustration can coexist. High relevance to restraint: one expressive element is enough when the typography is controlled.
